description: `mode` is spelled here because the alternative is inheriting it. Mend's onboarding wizard defaults a whole ACCOUNT to Scan Only, which sets Renovate to `silent`: it scans, publishes to Mend's portal, and creates no pull request, no issue and no dependency dashboard. Nothing in this repository can see that setting, and nothing it does looks like a failure — which is why the one time it bit, it read as a healthy tracker for thirty-two days and was found by somebody chasing a Dependabot alert rather than by a check. Silent also takes lockFileMaintenance with it, and that is the only mechanism that adopts a fix for a lockfile-only transitive advisory (see the entry on it below). A default nobody in the tree can read is a default that will be wrong again, so the repository asserts it rather than inheriting it.

Renovate performs the merge itself rather than handing the PR to GitHub's native auto-merge. The AI-reviewer ruleset requires a CodeRabbit status, and CodeRabbit skips bot-authored PRs SILENTLY — it posts no check at all, so there is nothing on the commit for the ruleset to be satisfied by — which is why the ruleset grants this app a bypass. Only the synchronous merge endpoint, the one Renovate calls on its own runs, consults that grant: GitHub's deferred auto-merge evaluator never re-reads bypass_actors, so under platformAutomerge a PR whose sole unsatisfied check is the bypassed one stays open forever however green it is. automergeSchedule admits a merge at any time, so a merge follows the run that first finds the branch green, instead of waiting for the nightly window that governs PR CREATION.

rebaseWhen is pinned to `conflicted` because the default `auto` resolves to `behind-base-branch` whenever automerge is on, and main takes ~70 commits a day: every open Renovate branch was force-pushed on roughly every merge, each force-push starting a full CI run that the next one cancelled. In one 5h42m sample, 80 of 200 CI runs were Renovate branches and 64 of those 80 ended `cancelled` — the fleet crowded out human PRs in the concurrency pool AND destroyed its own signal, since a cancelled run is indistinguishable from a red one. Rebasing-when-behind bought nothing to offset that: the main-required-status-checks ruleset sets strict_required_status_checks_policy false, so a behind-but-green branch is mergeable and Renovate merges it. The residual exposure — a dependency merged having been tested against a slightly older main — is the same one every human PR here already carries.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refreshes transitive packages, which have no manifest range for Renovate to raise. The repo-wide minimumReleaseAge does not apply here and is switched OFF explicitly — `minimumReleaseAge: 0` below — because a config option that inherits does not stop inheriting just because a description says it should not: Renovate delegates resolution to pnpm, so a 7-day floor here would hold back a whole lockfile refresh on the age of whichever transitive package moved most recently, which is the daily cadence silently becoming weekly-or-worse for the one mechanism that adopts a lockfile-only advisory fix. The age floor is enforced instead by pnpm 11's supply-chain policy at install time, which fails CI on a too-fresh entry and so blocks automerge. DAILY, not weekly, because this is the ONLY mechanism that adopts a fix for a lockfile-only transitive advisory: vulnerabilityAlerts cannot raise a package that has no manifest range, and Renovate removed the option that once bridged that gap. On a weekly cadence such a fix waited on the calendar rather than on the advisory — GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj (js-yaml, high) was fixed upstream twenty hours after a Monday run and would have sat unadopted for six more days. The cost is a lockfile PR whenever something in range moves, which automerges on green like any other.

debian-snapshot.description: Every timestamp snapshot.debian.org holds for the main archive, newest last. The CI image reads both the archive and its security half at one such timestamp, and snapshot resolves a timestamp to the newest import at or before it, so the main archive's list serves both.

debian-package.description: Every version of one binary package the archive has ever held, across all suites. The suite is not in the answer, so the allowedVersions rule below is what keeps a pin inside Debian 13.

customManagers.description: The Makefile pins six SBOM tools by digest, each with its tag in a trailing comment. Renovate has no manager for a Makefile, so without this one none of the six is ever offered an update: syft sat on v1.50.0 after v1.51.1 fixed the two-document pnpm-lock read. The digest is what runs and the comment is what a reader checks, so both move together or the comment starts lying.

docs/how-to/add-an-extension.md shows a go.mod verbatim, and whoever writes the next extension copies it — so the version in that fence is a pin like any other, and goversionpins_test.go holds it as one. No manager owns a fenced block, which is why the bump reached everything else and left the how-to a patch behind.
The CI image's snapshot timestamp. Every package pin below resolves inside it, so the Debian group moves it in the same branch as they move.

Each apt package the CI image installs, pinned `name=version` on a line of its own. The pattern is held to that one file, so the product Dockerfile is never read for Debian pins. backend/gates/ciimagepins_test.go runs this pattern over the Dockerfile and fails on a pin it does not reach.

packageRules.description: js-yaml stays on the 4.x line, and this is the only place that can say so. The override in pnpm-workspace.yaml exists solely to lift @redocly/openapi-core's EXACT js-yaml pin — 4.3.1 today — to 4.3.2, for GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj and GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh; Renovate reads that override as an ordinary range and offers the major like any other range it manages. Taking the major breaks the build instead of the advisory: openapi-typescript 7.x — latest — depends on @redocly/openapi-core ^1.34.6, which reads `js-yaml`'s `types.merge`, removed in 5.x, so `openapi-typescript` dies on require and fe-typecheck-composed fails with no schema to check against. @redocly/openapi-core 2.x is written against js-yaml ^5.2.2, so this rule and the override both go away together, once openapi-typescript adopts that line.

A major needs a human to read the changelog, so it can never satisfy automerge on its own and its branch would otherwise sit open indefinitely — the one shape that pays the rebase cost forever while having no path to merge. `conflicted` above still rebases a lockfile major on every main merge that touches the lockfile (24 of the last 100 did), so majors are pinned to `never`: the branch goes stale, which is the correct state for a change waiting on a contact. Whoever picks it up rebases it by ticking the PR's own checkbox.

The go directive and `.tool-versions` move in ONE pull request, because the gate that holds them (backend/gates/goversionpins_test.go) compares fifteen pins against each other and a half-moved tree fails it. This group used to be impossible: gomod's `golang` depType was disabled, so the asdf manager bumped `.tool-versions` alone, every other pin stayed behind, and the gate took `deterministic-gates` and through it `ci` red on every open pull request the moment it was rebased. It happened twice. Grouping is what makes the half-moved state unreachable rather than merely visible; the custom manager below carries the two files no manager owns. The dockerfile manager is in it because the release image and the CI image each copy Go from a golang image, and the same gate reads both tags.

A go MINOR raises the language floor every module compiles against, which is a decision somebody makes rather than a version that moved — the tree's own floor changes have been deliberate commits. So it never satisfies automerge, and `never` keeps its branch from paying the rebase cost forever while having no path to merge, exactly as the lockfile-major rule above does. A PATCH still automerges on green, which is the case this group exists for.

The documented supported Redis range tops out at 7.2 (docs/reference/system-requirements.md) — 7.4 left the BSD license family — and the version CI tests must stay inside the range operators are told to run. This cap blocks the 7.4/8.x tag bumps Renovate would otherwise raise; digest updates within the 7.2 tag still flow, which is how 7.2.x patch releases arrive.

TypeScript stays below 7 until the native compiler ships a stable JS API. The frontend's design-system and contract gates parse source through the `typescript` module's compiler API (createSourceFile, forEachChild, SyntaxKind); 7.x exports only a version stub plus `unstable/*` entry points, so taking it fails every one of those gates rather than the typecheck. Lift this cap in the same change that moves the gates onto 7's API once it is stable.

A Docker digest carries no release date, so the seven-day floor has nothing to count from. Under Renovate's default `timestamp-required` that update is never old enough: its `renovate/stability-days` status stays pending forever, its PR never automerges, and it holds a `prConcurrentLimit` slot for good. Five such PRs filled the limit and stopped every other update for two weeks, lockFileMaintenance included. `timestamp-optional` lets an undated update through. The floor never measured these updates, it only ever blocked them, and a digest moves only inside a tag this tree already pins.
A GitHub runner image carries no release date either, for the reason the digest rule above gives.

Only a Debian 13 version, from a datasource that lists every suite. A stable or security update carries `+deb13uN` or `~deb13uN`, and a version without it is either the one trixie released with or another release's, so the pin moves only when Debian ships a trixie update for it. Checked against the archive: make 4.4.1-2 and python3 3.13.5-1 carry no suffix and are offered nothing newer, while libnss3 moves from 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 to +deb13u5 and never to sid's 2:3.132-1.

The snapshot timestamp and every package pin move in ONE branch, because a version newer than the snapshot is one apt cannot find, and the build fails on it. separateMajorMinor is off because the timestamp's versioning reads a new day as a major, which would otherwise split the date from the packages; automerge and rebaseWhen are restated for the same reason, since the rule for majors above would hold a date bump for a human. Weekly, because snapshot imports four times a day and the nightly window would open a Debian branch, and an image rebuild, on every run. The age floor is off: neither datasource carries a release date, the floor would hold both pins forever, and a floor on one but not the other points a version past its snapshot. Debian's stable release managers and security team are the review a trixie update has already had.

The CI image's Debian base joins the same group, so a new base digest is tested with the snapshot and the pins it is upgraded to. It stays on 13: a new major moves every package pin at once, which is a human's change.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Advisory-driven PRs, unscheduled so they are not held to the nightly window. This reaches only packages with a manifest range of their own: an advisory naming a LOCKFILE-ONLY transitive package has nothing here for Renovate to raise, and no option restores that — `transitiveRemediation` was removed from Renovate and is stripped by config migration. lockFileMaintenance above is the only mechanism that adopts those, which is why its cadence is the security lever rather than anything in this block.
